annotation.title_clean: O. Reg. 306/15: Pilot Project - Automated Vehicles (under Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8)
annotation.title_en: O. Reg. 306/15: Pilot Project - Automated Vehicles (under Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8)
annotation.summary_en: Ontario regulation under the Highway Traffic Act establishing a pilot project for testing SAE Level 3–5 automated vehicles and co-operative truck platooning on public highways. It requires Registrar approval, high insurance coverage, driver takeover mechanisms, collision reporting and record keeping. Driverless testing is allowed under conditions. The regulation is revoked in October 2027.
key_provisions_or_claims: Automated vehicles (SAE Level 3-5) may be driven on highways only by approved owners for pilot testing purposes
Owners must carry liability insurance of at least $5M ($8M for vehicles seating 8 or more passengers); owners/lessees are liable for damage caused by driverless operation
Automated driving systems must include engage/disengage controls, failure alerts, driver takeover and a safe-stop fallback
Drivers must stay in the driver's seat and monitor the vehicle, except for Level 4-5 vehicles operating without a driver
Collisions must be reported to the Registrar within 10 days, and records must be kept and provided for the Minister's evaluation
